articles.title: Unitree targets $9 billion valuation in landmark IPO as humanoid robot race accelerates
articles.summary: Unitree has priced a Shanghai STAR Market IPO valuing the Chinese humanoid robotics company at about $9 billion, with plans to raise roughly $900 million for robot hardware, software, new products, and manufacturing expansion. The listing gives public-market investors one of the first direct exposures to a humanoid robotics manufacturer, even as profitability has weakened due to higher R&D and marketing spend and US-China technology restrictions create market-access risk.
articles.advisor_relevance: This matters because it shows investor appetite for physical AI and humanoid robotics moving from private speculation toward public-market financing. Unitree's revenue growth, planned manufacturing expansion, and strategic investment from DeepSeek point to accelerating commercialization, while margin pressure and regulatory risk highlight the capital intensity and geopolitical uncertainty around the sector.

articles.title: Tencent Cloud Open-Sources TencentDB Agent Memory v2.0: A Team-Level Memory Hub for AI Coding Agents

articles.title: Tacta Systems takes aim at high-skilled manufacturing work with TactaBot

articles.title: Stanford Evo 2 AI model generates phages against E. coli
articles.summary: Stanford researchers used the open-source Evo 2 generative AI model to generate thousands of candidate phage genomes, chemically synthesising nearly 300 and identifying 16 with strong E. coli-killing activity. The work shows AI can propose entire viable viral genomes, but still depends on computational filtering, DNA synthesis, and lab testing to validate results.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early but concrete example of generative AI moving from sequence design into physical laboratory validation. For advisors, the main read-through is not immediate commercialization, but the longer-term potential for AI to reshape biotech R&D workflows, increase demand for DNA synthesis and testing infrastructure, and raise governance questions around open-source biological design tools.
